escapes.plausible_wrong_implementation: Publish a syntactically valid handoff copied from another candidate so its issue source or material head does not describe the code being handed off.

literal_case.procedure: Bind the readiness package to the current exact issue source and new material head.
literal_case.evidence: The source hash was rebuilt exactly and all readiness matrices use the new material head.

sibling_cases.evidence: The exact Issue 587 source hash was reproduced.
All head-bound artifacts use the new material head.

prevention_change.evidence: A new material change invalidated the old certificate and triggered a full handoff rebuild.

detection_change.evidence: Terminal validation will require the published child parent to equal the certified material head.

escapes.plausible_wrong_implementation: Claim fallback and precedence coverage while the visible selector uses a generic or stale lower-priority value in one branch.

literal_case.procedure: Exercise a legacy-only record and a deliberately conflicting hybrid record.
literal_case.evidence: Repository regressions remain unchanged and distinguish legacy fallback from structured precedence.

sibling_cases.evidence: Structured values suppress contradictory legacy text.
Legacy-only edit leaves structured inputs empty.

prevention_change.evidence: Legacy-only and hybrid fixtures remain in the repository.

detection_change.evidence: Attack matrix retains the passed hybrid precedence control.

escapes.plausible_wrong_implementation: Approve a form because markup and payload tests pass while a legitimate browser POST is rejected earlier by an authentication or CSRF boundary.

literal_case.procedure: Exercise local authenticated mutation-origin equivalence with the same loopback aliases users can employ to reach the development server.
literal_case.evidence: Focused harness passes localhost, IPv4 loopback and IPv6 loopback while preserving protocol/port restrictions.

sibling_cases.evidence: A non-loopback hostname remains rejected even on the configured port.

prevention_change.evidence: Local loopback aliases are canonicalized narrowly rather than bypassing Origin validation.

detection_change.evidence: New repository test covers allowed loopback aliases and negative rejection cases.

escapes.plausible_wrong_implementation: Fix a reported local Origin failure by adding only the hostname that reproduced once, leaving LAN, bind addresses, containers, forwarded ports or HTTPS tunnels rejected by the same boundary.

literal_case.procedure: Exercise authenticated development mutation Origins across loopback, bind address, LAN and HTTPS tunnel-style hosts while retaining productive exact-match checks.
literal_case.evidence: Focused harness passes representative forwarded development origins and rejects malformed/missing values and productive mismatches.

sibling_cases.evidence: 0.0.0.0 and LAN-style HTTP origins are accepted when the configured APP_ORIGIN is local.
HTTPS tunnel-style origins, including an alternate port, are accepted in the local compatibility path.
Production and non-local configured APP_ORIGIN values still require exact origin equality.

prevention_change.evidence: The implementation keys compatibility to a local configured APP_ORIGIN instead of enumerating every possible browser access alias.

detection_change.evidence: Repository regression now includes LAN, bind-address, tunnel, malformed/missing and productive mismatch cases.
